title: Chapter 30. Nagari Padas — IV: the "Narahari" padas of GPT (sect. 3.2, nos. 94–110, 120–123)
html:
On what nagari-bhava is, the position of the tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) and the rules of translation, see the introductory note to the section of nagari padas in chapter 27; on the two poets named Narahari (Narahari Sarakara and Narahari Chakravarti) and on the attribution labels ("probably Sarakara", "probably Chakravarti", "not established"), see the introductory note to the "Narahari" appendix in chapter 17.

1. Narahari — "śuna śuna ago parāṇa soi…" (GPT1 p. 194, no. 94; GCC 7.10)

Nagari-bhava. A townswoman complains to her friend about her household: whenever she sighs and murmurs "Gora", her mother-in-law burns with anger, her sister-in-law is like poison, the neighbours taunt her day and night, she lives like a bird in a cage; but yesterday the Creator took pity — at the close of day Gaura passed along their street, and she secretly saw Him from the window: His face, brows, eyes, garland, gait; and the pain of her heart only doubled. Raga "yatharaga". Attribution: probably Chakravarti — GCC, kirana 7, pada 10.1

শুন শুন অগো পরাণ সোই । বেথিত জানিয়া তোমারে কই ॥

śuna śuna ago parāṇa soi | bethita jāniyā tomāre kai ||

śuna śuna ago — listen, listen; parāṇa soi — friend of my heart; bethita jāniyā — knowing you feel my pain; tomāre kai — I tell you

1.1Listen, listen, friend of my heart: I know you feel my pain — so to you I will tell it.

দেশের বাহির ঘরের রীত । সে কথা কহিতে কাঁদয়ে চিত ॥

deśera bāhira gharera rīta | se kathā kahite kām̐daye cita ||

deśera bāhira — beyond the custom of the land, unheard of; gharera rīta — the ways of the house; se kathā kahite — telling of it; kām̐daye cita — the heart weeps

1.2The ways of our house are unheard of in the land: as I tell them, my heart weeps.

গোরা বলি যদি নিশ্বাস ছাড়ি । শুনিয়া কোরধে জ্বলয়ে বুড়ী ॥

gorā bali yadi niśvāsa chāṛi | śuniyā koradhe jvalaye buṛī ||

gorā bali — saying "Gora"; yadi niśvāsa chāṛi — if I sigh; śuniyā — hearing; koradhe jvalaye — burns with anger; buṛī — the old woman (mother-in-law)

1.3If only I sigh, murmuring "Gora", the old woman hears and burns with anger.

ননদী বিষম বিষের প্রায় । তার গুণে প্রাণ দহিয়া যায় ॥

nanadī biṣama biṣera prāya | tāra guṇe prāṇa dahiyā yāya ||

nanadī — sister-in-law; biṣama biṣera prāya — like deadly poison; tāra guṇe — through her "virtues"; prāṇa dahiyā yāya — life burns away

1.4My sister-in-law is like deadly poison: through her "virtues" my life is burnt away.

পড়সি কেবল কুলের কাঁটা । দিবস রজনী দেয় যে খোঁটা ॥

paṛasi kebala kulera kām̐ṭā | dibasa rajanī deya ye khom̐ṭā ||

paṛasi — the neighbours; kebala — nothing but; kulera kām̐ṭā — thorns to the family's good name; dibasa rajanī — day and night; deya ye khom̐ṭā — they taunt

1.5The neighbours are nothing but thorns to a good name: day and night they prick me with taunts.

কারে দিব অগো ইহার সাখী । ঘরে থাকি যেন পিঞ্জরে পাখী ॥

kāre diba ago ihāra sākhī | ghare thāki yena piñjare pākhī ||

kāre diba ago — whom, friend, shall I give; ihāra sākhī — as witness to this; ghare thāki — I stay at home; yena piñjare pākhī — like a bird in a cage

1.6Whom, friend, shall I call to witness this? I stay at home like a bird in a cage.

সে সব কাহিনী কি কব আর । কহিতে দুখের নাহিক পার ॥

se saba kāhinī ki kaba āra | kahite dukhera nāhika pāra ||

se saba kāhinī — all those tales; ki kaba āra — what more shall I say; kahite — in the telling; dukhera nāhika pāra — there is no end to sorrow

1.7What more shall I tell of all this? There is no end to my sorrow.

গতদিন বিধি সদয় মোরে । আকাশের চাঁদ দিলেক করে ॥

gatadina bidhi sadaya more | ākāśera cām̐da dileka kare ||

gatadina — yesterday; bidhi sadaya more — the Creator was kind to me; ākāśera cām̐da — the moon of the sky; dileka kare — gave into my hand

1.8But yesterday the Creator was kind to me — he put the moon of the sky into my hand.

দিবা অবসানে গৌররায় । আমাদের পথে চলিয়া যায় ॥

dibā abasāne gaurarāya | āmādera pathe caliyā yāya ||

dibā abasāne — at the close of day; gaurarāya — Gaura Raya; āmādera pathe — along our street; caliyā yāya — goes walking

1.9At the close of day Gaura Raya was walking along our street.

তরাতরি গিয়া গবাক্ষদ্বারে । অলখিত হৈয়া দেখিনু তারে ॥

tarātari giyā gabākṣadvāre | alakhita haiyā dekhinu tāre ||

tarātari giyā — going in haste; gabākṣa-dvāre — to the window; alakhita haiyā — unseen; dekhinu tāre — I saw Him

1.10Hurrying to the window, unseen, I saw Him.

কিবা সে মধুর বদনচাঁদ । তরুণীগণের হৃদয়ফাঁদ ॥

kibā se madhura badanacām̐da | taruṇīgaṇera hṛdayaphām̐da ||

kibā se madhura — how sweet is that; badana-cām̐da — moon of a face; taruṇī-gaṇera — of young women; hṛdaya-phām̐da — a snare for hearts

1.11How sweet is that moon of a face — a snare for the hearts of young women!

ভুরুযুগ বড় ভঙ্গিম ছাঁদে । কে আছে এমন ধৈরজ বাঁধে ॥

bhuruyuga baṛa bhaṅgima chām̐de | ke āche emana dhairaja bām̐dhe ||

bhuruyuga — the pair of brows; baṛa bhaṅgima chām̐de — so gracefully curved; ke āche emana — who is there who; dhairaja bām̐dhe — can hold his composure

1.12The curve of His brows is so graceful — who has the composure to bear it?

খঞ্জন জিনিয়া নয়ান নাচে । বুঝিনু তাহাতে কেহ না বাঁচে ॥

khañjana jiniyā nayāna nāce | bujhinu tāhāte keha nā bām̐ce ||

khañjana jiniyā — outdoing wagtails; nayāna nāce — the eyes dance; bujhinu — I understood; tāhāte keha nā bām̐ce — from them no one escapes

1.13His eyes, outdoing wagtails, dance — I understood: from them no one escapes.

গলায় দোলয়ে কুসুমদাম । তা হেরি মূরছে কতেক কাম ॥

galāya dolaye kusumadāma | tā heri mūrache kateka kāma ||

galāya dolaye — sways at the throat; kusuma-dāma — a garland of flowers; tā heri — seeing it; mūrache kateka kāma — many a Kamadeva swoons

1.14A garland of flowers sways at His throat — seeing it, many a Kamadeva swoons.2

শোভা অপরূপ কি কব আর । ভুবনমোহন গমন তার ॥

śobhā aparūpa ki kaba āra | bhubanamohana gamana tāra ||

śobhā aparūpa — wondrous beauty; ki kaba āra — what more shall I say; bhubana-mohana — enchanting the world; gamana tāra — His gait

1.15What more shall I say of that wondrous beauty? His gait enchants the world.

তিলেক দেখিতে পাইনু সেথা । বাড়িল দ্বিগুণ হিয়ার ব্যথা ॥

tileka dekhite pāinu sethā | bāṛila dviguṇa hiyāra byathā ||

tileka — for a moment; dekhite pāinu sethā — I could see Him there; bāṛila dviguṇa — grew twofold; hiyāra byathā — the pain of the heart

1.16For only a moment could I see Him there — and the pain of my heart grew twofold.

নরহরি কহে দুখ না রবে । মনের মতন সকলি হবে ॥

narahari kahe dukha nā rabe | manera matana sakali habe ||

narahari kahe — Narahari says; dukha nā rabe — sorrow will not remain; manera matana — as the heart wishes; sakali habe — all will come to pass

1.17Narahari says: sorrow will not remain — all will come to pass as your heart desires.3

Nos. 94–99 of this chapter continue the 7th kirana of GCC — the townswomen of Navadvipa telling their friends in the morning (beginning — chapter 29, nos. 14–21): GCC 7.10–7.12 = nos. 94–96, 7.14–7.16 = nos. 97–99; GCC 7.13 (how a townswoman remembered Gaura while cooking) was not taken into GPT. GCC pp. 73–80 were checked against the scan (PDF pp. 78–85; re-OCRed with tesseract); pp. 81–88 (GCC 7.17–7.28) are missing from the only available scan (see n. 18). GCC readings: "parāṇa sai" (so also GPT2), "deya e khom̐ṭā", "bhuruyuga bara bhaṅgima chānde". Metre — short payar (a couplet to a line). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27). (cf. Krishna's name Madana-mohana, "He who enchants Madana himself"). afar (cf. nos. 2–3 and 5).

2. Narahari — "ki baliba ago gharera kathā…" (GPT1 pp. 195–196, no. 95; GCC 7.11)

Nagari-bhava. A townswoman's story: yesterday morning her mother-in-law went out, leaving her with her sister-in-law; the latter picked a quarrel and went off in a huff to the neighbours; alone at the window, the townswoman saw Gaura passing and threw Him a withered kumuda bud; Gora, taking it, said to the flower: "Do not grieve — the moon will rise"; at His glance she lost all strength; to her mother-in-law, on her return, she complained of her sister-in-law and explained her agitation by fatigue and fear — and the mother-in-law comforted her and scolded the sister-in-law. Raga "yatharaga". Attribution: probably Chakravarti — GCC, kirana 7, pada 11.4

কি বলিব অগো ঘরের কথা । সে সব শুনিলে পাইবে বেথা ॥

ki baliba ago gharera kathā | se saba śunile pāibe bethā ||

ki baliba ago — what shall I say, friend; gharera kathā — of the house; se saba śunile — if you hear it all; pāibe bethā — you will feel pain

2.1"What shall I say, friend, of what goes on in our house? If you hear it, it will pain you too.

কালি সুপ্রভাত হইল নিশি । বিরলে দেখিনু গৌরশশী ॥

kāli suprabhāta haila niśi | birale dekhinu gauraśaśī ||

kāli — yesterday; suprabhāta haila niśi — the night became a bright morning; birale — in secret; dekhinu — I saw; gaura-śaśī — the Moon Gaura

2.2Yesterday, as soon as night gave way to a bright morning, I secretly saw the Moon Gaura.

মরুক এখন লাজে কি করে । সে কাহিনী কিছু কহি তোমারে ॥

maruka ekhana lāje ki kare | se kāhinī kichu kahi tomāre ||

maruka ekhana — let it perish now; lāje ki kare — what can shame do; se kāhinī kichu — something of that tale; kahi tomāre — I tell you

2.3Perish shame now — what can it do to me? Something of it I will tell you.

আমারে রাখিয়া ননদী স্থানে । শাশুড়ী গেলেন সে পাড়া পানে ॥

āmāre rākhiyā nanadī sthāne | śāśuṛī gelena se pāṛā pāne ||

āmāre rākhiyā — leaving me; nanadī sthāne — with my sister-in-law; śāśuṛī gelena — my mother-in-law went; se pāṛā pāne — towards that quarter

2.4Leaving me with my sister-in-law, my mother-in-law went off to the other end of the village.

এথা ননদিনী করিল দ্বন্দ্ব । কহিল আমারে অনেক মন্দ ॥

ethā nanadinī karila dvandva | kahila āmāre aneka manda ||

ethā — and here; nanadinī karila dvandva — my sister-in-law picked a quarrel; kahila āmāre — said to me; aneka manda — many bad things

2.5And here my sister-in-law picked a quarrel and said many bad things to me,

নিজ জিত লাগি সকল ছাড়ি । রুষিয়া গেলেন পরের বাড়ী ॥

nija jita lāgi sakala chāṛi | ruṣiyā gelena parera bāṛī ||

nija jita lāgi — to have her own way; sakala chāṛi — leaving everything; ruṣiyā gelena — went off in anger; parera bāṛī — to someone else's house

2.6and, to have her own way, she dropped everything and went off in a huff to someone else's house.

একাকিনী মুই রহিনু ঘরে । বসিনু যাইয়া গবাক্ষদ্বারে ॥

ekākinī mui rahinu ghare | basinu yāiyā gabākṣadvāre ||

ekākinī mui rahinu ghare — I stayed at home alone; basinu yāiyā — I went and sat; gabākṣa-dvāre — by the window

2.7I stayed at home alone; I went and sat by the window.

গৌররূপগুণ ভাবিয়া মনে । চাহিয়া রহিনু পথের পানে ॥

gaurarūpaguṇa bhābiyā mane | cāhiyā rahinu pathera pāne ||

gaura-rūpa-guṇa — Gaura's beauty and virtues; bhābiyā mane — thinking in my mind; cāhiyā rahinu — I kept gazing; pathera pāne — at the road

2.8Thinking of Gaura's beauty and virtues, I kept my eyes on the road.

হেনই সময়ে গৌরাঙ্গসখা । আমাদের পথে দিলেন দেখা ॥

henai samaye gaurāṅgasakhā | āmādera pathe dilena dekhā ||

henai samaye — at that very moment; gaurāṅga-sakhā — Gauranga, the dear friend; āmādera pathe — in our street; dilena dekhā — appeared

2.9And at that very moment Gauranga, the dear friend, appeared in our street.

অলখিত লখি ও চাঁদমুখ । বিসরিনু কিছু হিয়ার দুখ ॥

alakhita lakhi o cām̐damukha | bisarinu kichu hiyāra dukha ||

alakhita lakhi — gazing unseen; o cām̐da-mukha — at that moonlike face; bisarinu kichu — I forgot a little; hiyāra dukha — the sorrow of my heart

2.10Gazing unseen at that moonlike face, I forgot a little of the sorrow of my heart.

তুরিতে মলিন কুমুদকলি । গবাক্ষের পথে দিলাম ফেলি ॥

turite malina kumudakali | gabākṣera pathe dilāma pheli ||

turite — at once; malina kumuda-kali — a withered kumuda bud; gabākṣera pathe — through the window; dilāma pheli — I threw

2.11At once I threw a withered kumuda bud through the window.

তা দেখিয়া গোরা চতুর অতি । করে লৈয়া কহে কুমুদ প্রতি ॥

tā dekhiyā gorā catura ati | kare laiyā kahe kumuda prati ||

tā dekhiyā — seeing it; gorā catura ati — Gora, very quick-witted; kare laiyā — taking it in His hand; kahe kumuda prati — says to the kumuda

2.12Seeing it, Gora — and He is very quick-witted — took it in His hand and says, speaking to the kumuda:

চিন্তা নাহি শশী উদয় হবে । দিনকর-তাপ দূরেতে যাবে ॥

cintā nāhi śaśī udaya habe | dinakara-tāpa dūrete yābe ||

cintā nāhi — do not grieve; śaśī udaya habe — the moon will rise; dinakara-tāpa — the heat of the sun; dūrete yābe — will go far away

2.13'Do not grieve: the moon will rise, and the heat of the sun will go far away.'5

এত কহি হাসি নয়ান কোণে । বারেক চাহিল আমার পানে ॥

eta kahi hāsi nayāna koṇe | bāreka cāhila āmāra pāne ||

eta kahi — having said this; hāsi — smiling; nayāna koṇe — from the corner of His eye; bāreka cāhila — glanced once; āmāra pāne — towards me

2.14Having said this, smiling, He glanced just once from the corner of His eye towards me.

অমনি অবশ হইল তনু । বিষম সাপেতে দংশিল জনু ॥

amani abaśa haila tanu | biṣama sāpete daṃśila janu ||

amani — at once; abaśa haila tanu — the body lost its strength; biṣama sāpete — a deadly snake; daṃśila janu — as if had bitten

2.15At once my body lost all strength, as if a deadly snake had bitten me.

যতনে ধৈরজ ধরিতে নারি । মনে হয় গিয়া পরশ করি ॥

yatane dhairaja dharite nāri | mane haya giyā paraśa kari ||

yatane — try as I might; dhairaja dharite nāri — I cannot keep my composure; mane haya — I feel; giyā paraśa kari — to go and touch

2.16Try as I might, I could not keep my composure: I longed to go and touch Him.6

ঘন ঘন কাঁপি ঘামিল গা । উঠিয়া চলিতে না চলে পা ॥

ghana ghana kām̐pi ghāmila gā | uṭhiyā calite nā cale pā ||

ghana ghana kām̐pi — trembling again and again; ghāmila gā — the body sweated; uṭhiyā calite — rising to walk; nā cale pā — the feet do not move

2.17I tremble all over, my body sweats; I rise to walk — my feet will not move.

কি কহিব চিতে প্রবোধ দিয়া । রহিলাম অতি আতুর হৈয়া ॥

ki kahiba cite prabodha diyā | rahilāma ati ātura haiyā ||

ki kahiba — what shall I say; cite prabodha diyā — trying to calm my heart; rahilāma — I remained; ati ātura haiyā — in great agitation

2.18What shall I say? Trying to calm my heart, I remained in great agitation.

হেন কালে ঘরে শাশুড়ী আইলা । মোরে পুছে কেন এমন হৈলা ॥

hena kāle ghare śāśuṛī āilā | more puche kena emana hailā ||

hena kāle — just then; ghare śāśuṛī āilā — my mother-in-law came home; more puche — asks me; kena emana hailā — why are you like this

2.19Just then my mother-in-law came home and asks me: 'Why are you like this?'

মো অতি কাতরে কহিনু তারে । ননদী রহিতে না দিবে ঘরে ॥

mo ati kātare kahinu tāre | nanadī rahite nā dibe ghare ||

mo ati kātare — I very piteously; kahinu tāre — told her; nanadī — my sister-in-law; rahite nā dibe ghare — will not let me live in the house

2.20Very piteously I told her: 'My sister-in-law will not let me live in the house.

আপনি রহিলে কিছু না বলে । অনলের সম অন্তর জ্বলে ॥

āpani rahile kichu nā bale | analera sama antara jvale ||

āpani rahile — when you yourself are here; kichu nā bale — she says nothing; analera sama — like fire; antara jvale — her heart burns

2.21When you yourself are at home, she says nothing, but her heart burns like fire.

তুমি গেলা ঘর ছাড়িয়া সেথা । মো সনে কোন্দল করিল হেথা ॥

tumi gelā ghara chāṛiyā sethā | mo sane kondala karila hethā ||

tumi gelā — you went; ghara chāṛiyā sethā — leaving the house, there; mo sane — with me; kondala karila hethā — she quarrelled here

2.22You left the house to go there — and here she picked a quarrel with me.

সে কথা কহিতে নাহিক ওর । ইথে কিছু দোষ না ছিল মোর ॥

se kathā kahite nāhika ora | ithe kichu doṣa nā chila mora ||

se kathā kahite — in telling of it; nāhika ora — there is no end; ithe — in this; kichu doṣa nā chila mora — there was no fault of mine

2.23There is no end to the telling of it; and there was no fault of mine in it at all.

যদি মনে কোন সন্দেহ থাকে । তবে পুছ এই পড়সি লোকে ॥

yadi mane kona sandeha thāke | tabe pucha ei paṛasi loke ||

Summary of chapter 30

The chapter continues the padas signed "Narahari" from section 3.2 of GPT — the townswomen of Nadia telling their friends in the morning how, despite the strictness of their mothers-in-law, sisters-in-law, fathers-in-law and husbands, they saw Gaura. Nos. 94–99 (nos. 1–6) were found in Narahari Chakravarti's *Gaura-charita-chintamani (kirana 7, padas 10–12, 14–16; "probably Chakravarti" — B; no. 97 in GPT is only the second half of the GCC pada 7.14). Nos. 100–110 and 120–123 (nos. 7–21) stand in GPT in the place of GCC 7.17–7.28, but those pages (pp. 81–88) are lost in the only available scan of GCC, and there are no other witnesses: they are labelled "not established" (C), with a note on their probable origin in GCC (n. 18). In several padas the strict elders — a mother-in-law, a father-in-law, the husband's aunt — themselves lose their composure on hearing the kirtana or seeing Gaura and become His devotees (nos. 9, 13, 18); the direct motifs of attraction and of deceiving the elders are rendered exactly, with notes on the position of the tradition (introductory note, chapter 27).*
